Diagnostics of an fgls fit

Source: R/diagnostics.R
weight_diagnostics.Rd

  • weight_diagnostics(): how concentrated the FGLS weights \(1/\hat v_t\) are: the ratio of the largest to the smallest fitted variance, the Kish effective sample size \((\sum w)^2 / \sum w^2\) as a share of the sample, and the share of the total weight carried by the top 1% of observations.

  • ar_roots(): roots of the estimated lag polynomial \(1 - \hat\rho_1 z - \dots - \hat\rho_k z^k\); the filter is invertible when all lie outside the unit circle.

  • nonexogeneity_share(): the relative size of the first-stage correction of PG26 eq. (29), averaged over coefficients. Values near zero mean the regressors behave as exogenous; large values mean the naive variance (eq. 27) would understate the uncertainty.

Usage

weight_diagnostics(fit)

ar_roots(fit)

nonexogeneity_share(fit)

Arguments

fit

An "fgls" object (with a heteroskedasticity correction for weight_diagnostics(), a serial-correlation correction otherwise).

Value

A named numeric vector, a complex vector, or a number.

See also

Other diagnostics: adf_test(), test_predetermined()

Examples

fit <- fgls(y ~ x, data = simulate_combined(200, seed = 1), seed = 1)
weight_diagnostics(fit)
#>       variance_ratio    effective_n_share top1pct_weight_share 
#>           5.57109452           0.81246809           0.02399232 
Mod(ar_roots(fit))
#> [1] 1.897991
nonexogeneity_share(fit)
#> [1] 0.000919948
